extraction.name: AMASS: Archive of Motion Capture as Surface Shapes
extraction.description: AMASS is a large and varied database of human motion that unifies 15 different optical marker-based mocap datasets by representing them within a common framework and parameterization using the SMPL body model. It includes more than 40 hours of motion data, spanning over 300 subjects, more than 11,000 motions, and provides a consistent representation of human motion for animation, visualization, and generating training data for deep learning.
extraction.creator: Naureen Mahmood, Nima Ghorbani, Nikolaus F. Troje, Gerard Pons-Moll, Michael J. Black
extraction.publisher: Meshcapade GmbH, MPI for Intelligent Systems, York University, MPI for Informatics
extraction.citeAs: Naureen Mahmood, Nima Ghorbani, Nikolaus F. Troje, Gerard Pons-Moll, Michael J. Black. AMASS: Archive of Motion Capture as Surface Shapes. arXiv:1904.03278v1 [cs.CV], 2019.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: AMASS unifies 15 existing motion capture datasets by converting mocap data into realistic 3D human meshes using the SMPL body model. The data collection process involves fitting the SMPL model to sparse marker-based mocap data, capturing body shape, pose, and soft-tissue dynamics. The method works for arbitrary marker sets and recovers realistic hand motion. The dataset includes 42 hours of mocap data, 346 subjects, and 11,451 motions.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Physical data collection, Software Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: 15 existing motion capture datasets (e.g., CMU, MPI-HDM05, KIT, BioMotion Lab, ACCAD) with varying marker sets ranging from 37 to 91 markers. The datasets were publicly available or obtained privately.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The raw mocap data was processed using MoSh++, which fits the SMPL body model to the sparse markers. This involves two stages: Stage I estimates body shape and latent marker positions, while Stage II optimizes pose and soft-tissue deformations for each frame. Hyperparameters were tuned using the SSM dataset to minimize reconstruction error.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The annotations are derived from the SMPL body model parameters, including shape (16 dimensions), soft-tissue coefficients (8 dimensions), and pose parameters (90 dimensions, including hand articulations). The annotations are generated automatically by fitting the model to the mocap data.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: MoSh++, SMPL, DMPL, MANO hand model, Chumpy autodifferentiation package, Powells gradient-based dogleg minimization
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: AMASS is publicly available at http://amass.is.tue.mpg.de and will be continuously updated with new captures contributed by the research community. The dataset is supported by the authors for community contributions.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: AMASS inherits limitations from the original mocap datasets, such as variations in marker sets and laboratory-specific procedures. The dataset may not generalize well to motions or body shapes not represented in the original datasets. Additionally, the dataset does not include facial motion capture.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, and Fine-tuning for deep learning models in animation, visualization, and computer vision. The dataset is designed to generate synthetic training data for computer vision tasks and enable new applications requiring large amounts of training data.
